new_groups.label: Westminster, 26 November 1772: the King's speech opening the session: 'My Lords and Gentlemen, I should most willingly have consulted your private convenience, by allowing you a longer recess from business'
new_groups.definition: Printings of the King's speech to both Houses of Parliament at the opening of the session, 26 November 1772: 'My Lords and Gentlemen, I should most willingly have consulted your private convenience, by allowing you a longer recess from business, if I had not thought, that some very important parts of the public service required the immediate attention of Parliament ...' new_groups.label: New York, 4 February, and Philadelphia, 8 February 1773: 'By Captain Henshaw, from St. Vincents, we are informed that General Leybourne was gone to Grenada, and the command of the troops devolved on Col. Dalrymple, who had entirely surrounded the Indians'
new_groups.definition: Printings of a shipmaster's report from St. Vincent in two wordings, a New York paragraph of 4 February 1773 ('Wednesday the 27th ult. Capt. A shipmaster's report at second hand, as the papers reprinted it.

new_groups.label: London, 1773: 'The report that upwards of 200,000 people had been lost in the river Canton, in China, in a hurricane in August last, may seem extravagantly great'
new_groups.definition: Printings of a London paragraph of 1773 (the New England papers print '30,000' or 'thirty thousand' where the Virginia papers print '200,000'): 'The report that upwards of 200,000 people had been lost in the river Canton, in China, in a hurricane in August last, may seem extravagantly great; but when it is considered that the fishermen on that river, and all others that carry manure for the cultivation of rice, live with their families at all times in their boats, it may not appear so enormous ...'. A London report, as the papers reprinted it.
new_groups.admission_rule: Reviewed 1773 printings, checked against the scan.

new_groups.label: London, July 1773: 'great numbers of vessels from Dublin, Londonderry, Belfast, Learn, Cork, and other ports, have lately sailed or are soon expected to sail, full of passengers, for different parts of America'

dispositions_summary.method: The automatic families first printed in 1773 that reach 3 or more papers, and those of 1772 over the 1773 pages, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json: 274 items printed somewhere, 38 reaching 4 papers by the finder's counts; items_from_1772.json: 9). Every finder item in 3 or more papers was counted again by the first 40 words of its opening against every page of 1773 in both transcriptions (a page prints the item when it holds at least 18 of the opening's word 5-grams), and texts read from different printings were merged (189 texts, 31 at the bar by that count). For every text one paper short of the bar (132), the missing paper was looked for again on its pages, by the text's words (the best page within its weeks) and by its names (the pages holding three or more of its proper names, ranked by the share of the opening's words they hold), and the pages found were read. A sweep of seven-word sequences shared by 4 or more papers, over every page, found items the families miss (as X-1803-09): 339 clusters; the 140 that no counted item explains were read, and their single paragraphs counted. Every item read at the bar or one paper short of it was then counted by phrase searches of its own words over all 846 pages in both transcriptions, and every hit read (phrase_patterns.json, phrase_hits.json).
dispositions_summary.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (Y-THIN), as amended by the owner on 23 November 2026 (choice B1): an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks (those with a surviving issue between its first and last printing, and at least in the three weeks from its first printing), and by at least 4; items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted; the other eligible items are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news; digests are not admitted. Single paragraphs from runs of news are counted by their own words (C-09). In 1773 four papers survive in most weeks, so an item printed by all four is admitted: 48 items are admitted by the rule's first part, from January to November; 1 eligible item printed by four of the five papers of its weeks is chosen for December, a month the admitted items do not reach.
dispositions_summary.paper_counting: 1773 has 6 catalogue series, which are 6 papers: the Massachusetts Spy, or Thomas's Boston Journal (Boston; 40 issues, none between 16 April and 6 May, 17 June and 22 July, or 26 November and 16 December), the New-Hampshire Gazette and Historical Chronicle (Portsmouth; 53 issues), the two Virginia Gazettes printed at Williamsburg by Alexander Purdie and John Dixon (sn84024739; 52 issues) and by William Rind (sn84024741; 52 issues), Dunlap's Pennsylvania Packet (Philadelphia; 10 issues, from 25 October) and the Connecticut Courant (Hartford; one issue, 28 December). Papers in print in any three weeks: 4 in most of the year; 3 for items first printed from 18 June to 1 July; 5 from early October; 6 from 8 to 27 December.

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: The 49 admitted and chosen items, the 29 eligible items not chosen, the 3 for the owner and the 20 read below the bar were counted by phrase searches of their own words, every hit read; their papers are in counted_items.json.
counted_item_by_item.Paragraphs in runs of news: London, Boston, New York and Philadelphia news reached the papers in runs of short paragraphs, which the four papers reprinted in different orders and weeks apart. Each paragraph is counted by its own opening sentence (C-09): 34 of the 48 admitted items are single paragraphs or letters from such runs.
counted_item_by_item.One report in two wordings: Some reports reached the papers in two wordings, which are counted together as one item (C-02, as the Hamburg letter of 1772): Captain Henshaw's news from St. Vincent (a New York paragraph of 4 February and a Philadelphia one of 8 February), the letter from Annapolis, Sir Jeffery Amherst's swearing in, the Hotel Dieu, the emigration from the north of Ireland, the King's gifts at Portsmouth, Captain Eve's report from the Bay of Honduras, the King of Prussia and Hanover, and the armaments of the Emperor and the King of Prussia; the Massachusetts Spy prints the London paragraph on the Sheriffs of Middlesex's letter without its first sentence. Another account of the same event, in other words and with other facts, is another text: the New-Hampshire Gazette's account of the Lord Mayor's election in October is not counted with the London paragraph the others print.
counted_item_by_item.A document under two introductions: The South Carolina Commons House's resolutions answering Virginia's are printed under a Charlestown report of 13 July by three papers and under another Charlestown report, of 16 July, by Rind's Virginia Gazette; they are counted together (C-02, as 1793's list of the powers under two introductions).
counted_item_by_item.Pages that are not printings: The phrase searches also hit pages that only quote an item or print another text in its words (C-07): the two Houses' addresses answering the King's speech of 26 November 1772 and a paragraph quoting it; other assemblies' resolutions answering Virginia's of 12 March; later paragraphs on the Orphan House in Georgia; letters from Paris on the fire at the Hotel Dieu; a later paragraph on Lord William Campbell's patent; the Governor's message on the letters laid before the Massachusetts House. They are not counted.
counted_item_by_item.Repeated printings and a misfiled issue: The Custom-House notice of 15 December 1772 was printed three times by each paper; all twelve printings are in the ledger (as 1779 and 1782 keep repeated printings). Purdie and Dixon's Virginia Gazette of 11 March has its RevX transcriptions filed one page off (in the release's revx_page_map); the notice on its page 4 is cut from the CA text.
